about: Whether a run plan file is valid and in which order its nodes can run. `valid` is true when no finding has the severity error (notes are allowed). `waves` lists the nodes in waves, a wave being the nodes whose `after` are all in earlier waves, each wave sorted by id; it is empty when the nodes cannot be ordered (a node without a usable id, an `after` that names no node, a cycle). `findings` are sorted: errors first, then by code, nodes and path. `digest` is sha256: and the 64 hex digits of the bytes read. `project` and `target_feature` are null when the plan gives no usable one; `nodes` is the number of entries of the plan's `nodes` list (0 when it is not a list). The verb exits 0 when the plan is valid and 1 when it is not, and prints the document in both cases; a file that cannot be read exits 2 with one line on standard error and no document, and a document that fails the check of this registry file exits 70 with one line on standard error and no document.
writes: Nothing: no state, no token, no network, no file; the plan, the roles qargi knows and the files a done command names are only read.

waves.description: The nodes in a valid run order, wave 1 first.

code.description: A stable word naming the rule: invalid-json, duplicate-json-key, too-large, not-an-object, unknown-key, missing-key, wrong-kind, wrong-schema, bad-value, empty-nodes, too-many-nodes, bad-id, duplicate-id, unknown-role, bad-scope, bad-done, bad-review-kind, bad-after, unknown-after, self-after, cycle, scope-overlap-unordered, review-requested. A reader goes by `severity`, not by a code it does not know.

severity.description: An error makes the plan invalid; a note does not.

nodes.description: The ids of the nodes the finding is about, sorted; empty when it is about the plan or about a node with no usable id.

path.description: Where in the plan, JSONPath-like ($.nodes[2].scope[0]); $ for the plan as a whole.

patterns.x-when: The code is scope-overlap-unordered: the first pair of scope entries, one of each of the two nodes in the order of `nodes`, that can touch the same path.

cycle.x-when: The code is cycle: one cycle in which every node comes after the next and the last after the first.
